content: Ampicillin-sulbactam, marketed as UNASYN, is provided as a sterile powder for intravenous (IV) and intramuscular (IM) administration. The powder must be reconstituted using one of the compatible diluents specified in the product insert. After reconstitution, the solution should be allowed to stand to dissipate any foam, enabling visual inspection to confirm complete solubilization. For IV use, the recommended concentration of UNASYN ranges from 3 to 45 mg/mL, which corresponds to 2 to 30 mg/mL of ampicillin and 1 to 15 mg/mL of sulbactam. The reconstitution process involves adding the diluent in two separate aliquots in a controlled environment, such as a laminar flow hood. Initially, 50 mL of the diluent is added, and the vial is shaken to dissolve the powder. Subsequently, an additional 42 mL of diluent is added, and the vial is shaken again. The solution should then be allowed to stand to dissipate foam and permit visual inspection for complete dissolution. The final solution will have a concentration of approximately 100 mg/mL of ampicillin and 50 mg/mL of sulbactam. The vial closure should only be penetrated once after reconstitution, using a sterile transfer device or dispensing set that allows for accurate measurement of the solution. Once reconstituted, the solution must be used within two hours if stored at room temperature or within four hours if refrigerated. If the bulk reconstituted solution is stored at room temperature (20°C/68°F) for less than one hour before further dilution, the use periods for the diluted solutions, as specified in the product insert, apply. Any unused portions of the solution remaining after the specified time periods must be discarded. In laboratory animals, reversible glycogenosis was observed, which was dependent on both dose and duration of exposure. However, this phenomenon is not expected to occur at therapeutic doses and plasma levels achieved during the relatively short duration of combined ampicillin/sulbactam therapy in humans.
